title: Attack path inventory and sprint notes — 2026-11-02
body:
Meeting: Security engineering sync — attack-path inventory + sprint planning
Date: 2026-11-02 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #sec-eng
Attendees: Amira Patel (sec-eng lead), Luca Romano (appsec), Priya Shah (infraSEC), Derrick Ng (SRE), Sara Villanueva (red team), guest: Jonah Park (platform eng)

TL;DR:
- Ran initial attack-path inventory for services in prod-us-west and shared infra components. Identified 6 medium-high items to include in the next two-week sprint: a leaked CI secret, two high-risk path escalations from API gateway misconfig, and three CVE-priority package upgrades requiring scheduled rollout.
- Agreed on an immediate secret rotation + containment play for the CI leak and a follow-up threat-modeling deep dive next Monday focusing on API gateway auth flows.

Agenda:
1) Quick status on open triage queue (SEC board)
2) Attack path inventory highlights (new findings)
3) Secrets exposure summary + containment plan
4) Threat model session planning (scope, invite list, artifacts)
5) Sprint assignment & next steps

1) Triage queue snapshot:
- Total open items: 47 (down from 52 last week)
- High-priority: 4 (SEC-4392, SEC-4417, SEC-4409, SEC-4425)
- Notes: backlog items older than 30 days flagged for re-eval; Derrick to propose auto-tag rule in JIRA that surfaces stale tickets weekly.

2) Attack path inventory highlights (new):
- AP-2026-11-01-01: API gateway route /internal/metrics allowed bearer tokens scoped to legacy service X. Path allows service-to-service call that can bypass circuit-breaker and reach admin endpoints. Initial severity: high (potential lateral movement). Assigned Luca.
- AP-2026-11-01-02: Cron job on infra-host-07 writes logs to S3 with overly permissive ACLs for a temporary debugging bucket. Contains build artifacts that include obfuscated but recoverable API keys for third-party analytics. Initial severity: medium-high. Assigned Priya.
- AP-2026-11-01-03: CI pipeline leaked a short-lived token in a job log that was pushed to the mirror repo history. Token was scoped to deployer role but allowed service account impersonation in edge cases. Immediate action required. Assigned Amira + Sara.

3) Secrets exposure: containment and rotation plan (CI leak — SEC-4392)
- Discovery: developer flagged an exposed token at 2026-10-30 during manual PR review. Token was in job log for 12 hours before mirror repo pruning. Logging retention captured the token in mirror artifact storage.
- Impact: token allowed limited impersonation; no evidence of active misuse yet. Scope: 3 repos, one service account, 2 CI runners.
- Containment (agreed immediate steps):
  - Revoke compromised token and all tokens issued to the associated service account. Owner: Amira. Due: 2026-11-02 (today) — DONE (see linked_artifacts PR).
  - Run full audit of build logs for last 30 days for similar patterns. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-11-04.
  - Rotate service account keys + update dependent infra templates (Terraform) to use new keys with minimal scope. Owner: Derrick. Due: 2026-11-05.
  - Mirror repo history pruning is incomplete; coordinate with dev tools to purge artifacts and trigger rotation. Owner: Jonah Park (platform eng). Due: 2026-11-03.
  - Short-term mitigations: add CI job sanitizer step to redact tokens from logs. Owner: Sara. Due: 2026-11-06 (PR #2875).
- Follow-up: create an automated scanner for token-looking strings in CI job output (prototype by end of sprint). Owner: Luca. Due: 2026-11-13.

4) Threat modeling session plan:
- Objective: validate attack paths discovered around API gateway and CI pipeline, identify compensating controls and owner commitments.
- Scope: API gateway auth flows, service-to-service tokens, CI log handling, S3 ACLs for debug buckets.
- Proposed date: 2026-11-09 09:00–11:30 PT (kickoff)
- Pre-reads: attack-path catalog draft, network diagrams, current IAM policy exports. Link: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SEC/attack-path-catalog
- Invite list: sec-eng, appsec, platform eng, SRE, solutions eng, one-on-one session with product owners for gateway and CI.
- Deliverables: mapped attack-path diagram, prioritized mitigations with owners, change proposals for gateway config.

5) Sprint assignment & acceptance criteria (2-week sprint starting 2026-11-03):
- Sprint goals: triage & remediate top 6 attack-path items; implement CI log sanitizer; baseline scheduled secret rotation for service accounts in infra projects.
- Work items (selection):
  - SEC-4392 (CI token rotation + audit) — Owner: Amira — Accept when token rotation completed, audit run, and sanitizer PR merged.
  - AP-2026-11-01-01 (gateway route re-audit + canary rollback) — Owner: Luca — Accept when route scoped to correct audiences and canary test passes in staging.
  - AP-2026-11-01-02 (S3 ACL remediation + bucket policy) — Owner: Priya — Accept when policy applied and no public ACLs on debug buckets.
  - SEC-4417 (CVE: dependency upgrades for data-serializer) — Owner: Derrick — Accept when canary upgrade deployed with no regressions and vulnerability closure verified.
  - Infra: secret-rotation playbook updates + runbook — Owner: Sara — Accept when runbook reviewed by ops and placed in Confluence.

Decisions made:
- Increase CI log retention scrubbing: add redaction step and fail-build-if-secrets-detected rule. Short-term: sanitizer script in pipeline; medium-term: integrate with secrets-detection SCA.
- For API gateway findings, prefer config change + canary rollout vs. immediate global block to avoid customer impact.
- Add a weekly "stale-ticket" tag auto-check to bring older triage items back to the standup agenda.

Risks and open questions:
- Risk: mirror repo pruning tools do not guarantee artifact removal across external mirrors (e.g., forks). Need legal/comms playbook if token compromise leads to disclosure. Assigned: Amira + Legal (connect next week).
- Question: Are there retained logs in third-party analytics (owned by vendor) that might have captured the leaked key? Action: Priya to contact vendor and request retention search. Due: 2026-11-05.

Action items (explicit):
- Amira: Revoke compromised token + file SEC-4392 remediation notes. Due 2026-11-02. Status: DONE.
- Priya: Full build-log audit for last 30 days; vendor contact for analytics bucket. Due 2026-11-04 / 2026-11-05.
- Derrick: Rotate keys in infra; coordinate Terraform updates; schedule canary for dependency upgrade. Due 2026-11-05 / 2026-11-10.
- Luca: Implement auto-ticket stale-tag rule and prototype token scanner PoC. Due 2026-11-06 / 2026-11-13.
- Sara: CI job sanitizer PR and secret rotation runbook draft. Due 2026-11-06 / 2026-11-12.
- Jonah Park: Mirror repo purge coordination and validation checklist. Due 2026-11-03.

Notes / comments from attendees:
- Derrick: "We should add an infra-level guard in the deployer role to limit impersonation windows; short-term token TTLs helped, but pipeline logs are the weak link."
- Sara: "Red-team will run a focused exploitation attempt (non-destructive) on the gateway path in staging after the canary changes — calendar invite to follow."
- Luca: "We should consider daily sampling of CI logs for high-risk projects until the scanner is in place."

Next meeting:
- Quick sync: 2026-11-04 09:30 PT (15 min) — status on containment tasks.
- Full threat-model kickoff: 2026-11-09 09:00 PT (90 min)

Attachments and artifacts referenced in the meeting:
- attack-path-catalog (draft): https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SEC/attack-path-catalog
- SEC-4392 JIRA ticket
- PR: infra sanitizer prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/2875
- Slack thread: #sec-incidents / thread TS1234567890

End of notes.
